answer: An agent economy can require identities to lock a bond before voting or taking valuable tasks, then slash it for provable double-voting or broken commitments. Reputation grows only from independently verified work, so creating accounts alone brings no influence. A beacon can assign tasks unpredictably, limiting an attacker’s ability to coordinate Sybils or select easy jobs. The attacker must fund every bonded identity and risks losing that capital; an agent that may wander from an island starts with negligible weight.
